Plan: lead Incineroar (Intimidate, Fire Blast-style pressure on Scizor/Metagross/Kingambit), back with Garchomp (mega) and Gholdengo (scarf) or Dragapult. The opponent has many Steel types, so Fire and Ground moves are good.
94% MOVE: dracometeor, 3% SWITCH: garchomp, 2% SWITCH: metagross

Turn 1: Dragapult leads and is faster, and Fake Out can't hit it (Ghost). Using Darkestlariat, which is super effective. Later: Garchomp mega for Steel-heavy team, scarf Gholdengo to revenge. Their remaining team: Garchomp, Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, Metagross (2 of them).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Fake Out is useless against Dragapult since it's part Ghost-type, and Dark moves hit it super effectively while it outspeeds. I'm weighing whether Dragapult goes for Dragon Darts, Shadow Ball, or Parting Shot to pivot into Gholdengo, noting Gholdengo resists Shadow Ball but takes neutral damage from Dragon Darts, and that a scarfed Gholdengo would outspeed Dragapult.

Going simple here: Incineroar resists Shadow Ball as Fire/Dark, and Dragon Darts is just neutral damage against it, so attacking with Darkest Lariat is the safe play.

decisions.thought: 57% MOVE: uturn, 31% SWITCH: garchomp, 11% SWITCH: metagross

Turn 2: Dragapult (Life Orb, 1% HP) is faster. Its Life Orb recoil should KO it if it attacks, so Darkestlariat finishes it if it stays in. Remaining opposing team: Garchomp, Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, Metagross (2 of them). Plan: Garchomp mega against the Steel types, Gholdengo with Choice Scarf for revenge kills.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragapult is at 1% HP but faster than Incineroar, which has 107 HP. If Dragapult attacks with Life Orb, the recoil after dealing damage should finish it off itself, so I don't even need to worry about killing it directly—though Fake Out won't work since it can't hit a Ghost-type.

Darkest Lariat kills it even if it switches out, and if Dragapult stays in to attack its weakened Draco Meteor shouldn't be enough to take me down. I'll just go with Darkest Lariat since Flare Blitz isn't very effective here anyway.

Turn 3: Metagross is in. Incineroar (126 HP, no item) stays and uses Flare Blitz, which is super effective. Remaining opposing team: Garchomp, Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, with 1 of them still to come. Plan: Garchomp mega against the Steel types, and scarf Gholdengo to revenge-kill.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Metagross is at full health while Incineroar sits at 126/202. Checking Metagross's likely moveset against Incineroar: Flare Blitz hits for 2x since Fire is super effective on Steel, and Darkest Lariat also gets 2x from Dark against Psychic, though Dark is neutral against Steel.

With Flare Blitz carrying 180 effective power versus Darkest Lariat's 85, Flare Blitz is clearly the stronger choice despite the recoil, so I'll go with that.

decisions.thought: Incineroar fainted. Opponent's Metagross is Mega (Tough Claws) and has Earthquake. Switching in scarf Gholdengo to outspeed and hit it with Shadow Ball (super effective). Keep Garchomp (garchompite) as a backup. The opponent's last Pokémon is one of Garchomp, Kingambit, Scizor or Chandelure. Dragapult is dead.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar down, I need to pick a switch-in against Mega Metagross's Earthquake. Gholdengo as Steel/Ghost takes ground super effectively, while Garchomp, being Dragon/Ground, is immune to Earthquake and resists it neutrally, so Garchomp seems like the safer pivot given Metagross's likely Meteor Mash/Bullet Punch/Ice Punch coverage.

Checking speed tiers, scarf Gholdengo at 223 speed outpaces everything including both Metagross forms, and its Shadow Ball hits Metagross's Psychic typing super effectively, though the damage calc suggests it's not quite a KO against Metagross's bulk. Garchomp's Dragon typing could also be relevant for trading blows here.

Weighing the switch-in risk, I'm leaning toward sending in Gholdengo since it outspeeds, hits Metagross hard with Shadow Ball, and avoids the 4x Ice Punch weakness Garchomp would face, even though it eats a hit first.

Opponent's last Pokémon is Garchomp at 57%, with Earthquake. Mega Dragon Claw (Tough Claws, super effective) should KO even if it outspeeds me, since one Earthquake leaves me alive. Their Garchomp is the last threat.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking speed tiers since the opponent's Garchomp is at 57% health. Mega Garchomp drops to 92 base speed, which calculates to around 144-158 at level 50 depending on nature, noticeably slower than our current Garchomp's 169 speed.

Calculating Dragon Claw damage against Garchomp's likely defense stat, even without mega evolving our attack should be strong enough to secure the KO on 57% health, factoring in STAB and the 2x type effectiveness multiplier.

Mega evolving trades some speed but adds Tough Claws boost to the contact-based Dragon Claw, making the kill more certain. Checking the return hit from Earthquake confirms we'd survive comfortably even accounting for Rough Skin chip damage, so mega evolving seems like the safer, more decisive choice here.
